meta.title: SDKs · {brand}
meta.description: A Python SDK first, built and tested internally, on one shared core. A C interface for C++ and game engines is planned. Licence pending the owner's decision.

hero.heading: Python first. One shared core.
hero.lede: Every SDK records provenance the same way because every SDK uses the same core. Signal processing stays in the Python tools your lab already trusts.

sections.heading: Every run carries its provenance.
body: Open a recording, run a pinned pipeline version, and get a provenance handle that records every parameter, version and input hash.

lines: import {pkg} as nf            # Illustrative API, subject to change
print(run.provenance.id)          # every parameter, version and input hash

sections.heading: Languages, in order.
body: We build for the languages our users already work in, in the order they ask for them.

items.heading: Python
items.body: The first SDK, designed to work alongside MNE-Python, BIDS and NWB tooling. Not published yet.

items.heading: C and C++
items.body: A C interface on the shared core, with interoperability through LSL and BrainFlow.

items.heading: Unity and Unreal
items.body: Planned, on the same C interface.

evidence.text: MNE-Python had about 308,000 PyPI downloads in the month to 26 September 2026.

sections.heading: Open where it helps you.
body: The SDKs, the shared core, the format converters and the pipeline step library are planned as open source (Apache-2.0 proposed), pending the owner's decision. The hosted platform, including the consent ledger and model registry, is proprietary.
No SDK code is published yet.
